summary.headline: GSK Pharma Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 15% to INR924 crore and PAT 24% to INR253 crore, with growth led by innovation at 7% of sales.
summary.overview: Standalone sales grew 15% YoY to INR924 crore, with EBITDA up 17% and EBITDA margin up 50 bps, and PAT up 24% to INR253 crore (27.6% margin). Management said about 4-5 percentage points of headline growth came from a soft base after last year's CMO supply disruption, so underlying growth was about 9-10%. Innovation products (IP-protected) reached 7% of sales versus about 4% a year ago, contributing about 4 points of growth. PAT growth included a one-off dividend from subsidiary Biddle Sawyer; excluding it, PAT growth was about 17%. Spend-to-sales rose about 1 percentage point on front-loaded promotional investment ahead of the September quarter.

financial_highlights.value: improved ~50 bps YoY (management expects ~34% range for year)

financial_highlights.change: driven by pricing and product mix
vs ~4% last year; ~4 pts of headline growth
opex up ~36% YoY per analyst question; management confirmed deliberate front-loading

segments.name: General medicines (Gen Med)
segments.commentary: Grew in double digits and most brands outgrew the market per IQVIA, with EIs of 105-106. About 44-45% of the Gen Med portfolio is under price control. Gen Med is about 2,000 field staff.

segments.name: Vaccines
segments.commentary: Held private-segment leadership in pediatric vaccines. Shingrix grew about 65% in Q1, sells about 45,000-50,000 doses per quarter, and crossed INR100 crore on a MAT basis. A phasing issue in availability for a couple of vaccines is to be corrected in Q2.

segments.name: Specialty (respiratory, oncology)
segments.commentary: Nucala has about 600 active patients, with new patient starts roughly doubling YoY to about 100-120 a month. Trelegy Ellipta holds about 10,000-12,000 units a month despite about 10-12 generic launches of umeclidinium. Zejula and Jemperli together treat about 250-300 patients a quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; the stated objective is sustaining double-digit growth.
Opex/investment ratios expected to moderate in following quarters; S&A ratio to normalise toward historical levels through the year.
EBITDA margin expected to be roughly in the 34% range, similar to last year.
Q2 seasonal acute trends were said to be tracking in line with expectations, with June and July data supportive.
Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin, second-line RRMM) launch expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27 after DCGI approval.
Bepirovirsen (Hibsago) launch in India expected within three to four quarters.
Arexvy launch and upcoming Ojjaara expected within roughly 18-24 months.
Long-term ambition of INR8,000 crore top line in four to five years; established portfolio to grow 8-10%, with new launches providing the rest of the ~13% CAGR.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is local-for-local: own plant at Nashik (MIDC) plus about 20 contract manufacturers; all Gen Med products are made locally. Management sees no need for further local manufacturing beyond the current portfolio.

Field force of about 2,000 in Gen Med and 200 in established vaccines; about 40-45 people in oncology (medical oncology and hematology), with new hiring focused on areas of little or no presence such as liver disease.
Blended productivity about INR15-16 lakh per rep, up 5-6% this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry Q1 growth was about 13.5%, with volume growth around 2%; oncology was the fastest-growing Indian pharma segment at about 27%.
GSK Q1 blended volume growth was about 3-3.5%, price about 6%, and the balance from new introductions.
Acute therapies are about 60% of the Indian pharma market; Q2 (July-September) is the seasonal peak.
Supply chain: management said the worst is behind, after the CMO disruption, and that cost hardening on imported inputs from rupee depreciation has not yet hit margins.
Zejula is among the top five PARP inhibitors; Jemperli is the only approved immunotherapy in first-line endometrial cancer, which has about 17,000-19,000 new diagnoses a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the parent's restructuring focused on specialty hurt growth and India investment, given the Gen Med-heavy portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gen Med still grows in double digits and the parent's cost programme is a simplification effort; India was already restructured, and global trials are being brought to India to shorten launch lags.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the CMO-related lost Calpol sales have been recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst is behind, the supply chain has been stress-tested, and business continuity plans are being strengthened. It did not quantify recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How is reach into Tier 3/4 and rural areas ensured, given peers' distributor models?
qa_highlights.answer: A super-distributor manages some tail-end brands to reach mofussil interiors; no new operating model details were given beyond this.

qa_highlights.question: What are trends for the seasonal acute Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Trends since June are tracking in line with expectations; management expects Q2 broadly in line with its plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is the opex spike a one-off, and how should EBITDA margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend was deliberately front-loaded ahead of the September quarter (about 3,800 HCP events); ratios should moderate, and EBITDA margins are expected around 34%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on Blenrep and Bepirovirsen commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Blenrep approved by DCGI for second-line RRMM, launch Q2 or Q3 FY27 (about 7,000-8,000 second-line patients). Bepirovirsen launch in three to four quarters; pricing model still being worked out.

risks_watch: Opex intensity and S&A ratio normalisation: the Q1 spend spike must moderate in coming quarters to hold a ~34% EBITDA margin.
Imported input cost hardening from rupee depreciation, and post-West Asia cost pressure, could erode gross margin gains.
Sustainability of underlying growth, which was about 9-10% after the base effect, versus the 13-14% CAGR implied by the INR8,000 crore target.
Launch timing of Blenrep (Q2/Q3 FY27) and Bepirovirsen, and their commercial model for a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B.
Q1 PAT growth included a one-off dividend from Biddle Sawyer, so the underlying growth rate is about 17%.
Trelegy Ellipta and Nucala face generic and competitive pressure; monitor Trelegy units and Nucala patient growth.
key_quotes: I don't generally give forward-looking guidance.
Overall, the vaccines business has held its market leadership in the private segment
So yes, we are, we are on that road map, we are on that pathway to see how and when we can launch.
So the ratios are, investment ratios are higher this quarter, but we expect them to moderate and go back to our historical trends in the following quarters.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and the innovation pipeline, citing double-digit momentum, Shingrix, Nucala and oncology uptake. It was cautious on margins and guidance, declining formal guidance and conceding the Q1 opex spike, and it was evasive on Bepirovirsen pricing and the commercial model, deferring details to Q2.

growth.why: Management sustains an 8-10% medium-term growth objective and an INR8,000 crore top-line ambition in 4-5 years, backed by innovation launches (Blenrep Q2/Q3 FY27, Bepirovirsen within 3-4 quarters) and pricing, with no new capacity: Nashik plus contract manufacturers and management sees no need for further local manufacturing.
